rulings.challenge_claim: The rejected-alternative discussion names candidate chunking boundaries with the artifact term row instead of describing them by verse or literary unit; three clauses refer to a further row, the preceding row, and this row.
rulings.grounds: The three clauses are present as described, but the register rule they are measured against bars POSITIONAL row references and requires cross-row references to be VERSE-ANCHORED, and on that test only one of the three is a violation. 'Ending the preceding row later, at web:Isa.49.7' is a positional reference and is a genuine hit; 'Cutting a further row at web:Isa.49.10' names the artifact without naming a position, and 'letting this row begin only at web:Isa.49.9' is a self-reference, not a positional one; all three carry explicit verse anchors, which is what the rule actually demands. SCOPE, by census over the frozen corpus: positional row references stand at 32 occurrences in 24 of 225 rows, and the bare artifact noun at 526 occurrences in 170 of 225 rows, with the validator suite green throughout. This is therefore a corpus-wide register class, not a c22 defect, and four separate medium findings against it in one cluster overstate it; severity drops to low. The packet's own application is uneven: the last row of this cluster uses the artifact noun twice in its device_notes and was supported without a register challenge. The underlying seam is sound and byte-confirmed, exactly as the challenge concedes: oshb:Isa.49.8 opens כֹּ֣ה אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֗ה (byte), verse-initial and an inventoried divine frame, and the closing verse opens with a presentative, הִנֵּה אֵ֕לֶּה (oshb:Isa.49.12, byte); both of the row's splices are literal substrings of their cited verses at byte tier. One substantive point stands beside the register one and is byte-true: the strongest interior rival is never named, oshb:Isa.49.9 opening לֵאמֹ֤ר לַֽאֲסוּרִים֙ צֵ֔אוּ (byte), an infinitive of speech governing imperatives addressed to the bound, while the rival field reaches instead for the turn one verse later; that infinitive carries no independent frame token and is subordinate to the frame already opened, so it does not defeat the cut, but it is the candidate the field should have engaged.
rulings.remedy: Author-wave work order, register and disclosure only (no boundary change). (i) Replace the positional reference in P14-003.strongest_rejected_alternative with a verse-anchored content term; leave the two non-positional, verse-anchored clauses alone unless the owner pins a stricter convention, and run the change as ONE corpus-wide register pass over the 32 positional occurrences in 24 rows rather than as four c22 edits. (ii) Optionally strengthen the same field by naming the real interior rival with its bytes: לֵאמֹ֤ר לַֽאֲסוּרִים֙ צֵ֔אוּ (oshb:Isa.49.9), an infinitive of speech governing imperatives, subordinate to the frame opened at oshb:Isa.49.8 and carrying no independent frame token. Tests the cure must pass: no positional row reference survives in any field; every cross-row reference keeps its verse anchor; any newly spliced Hebrew re-collates at byte tier with the normalization dry-run clean; the ref-mirror check stays green with oshb:Isa.49.9 added if the rival is written in; the cross-row 7-gram gate stays green.

rulings.grounds: Upheld on both limbs, and the substitute warrant offered verifies exactly. The field reads that the isolable reading matches a doxology-closure pattern the campaign has recognised elsewhere in the book: an appeal to the reviewing project's own history that names no verse and shows no bytes, in the field that has to carry the rival warrant. That is the register class the standing purge bars and an evidence gap at the same time. The book's own text does carry the parallel: the comfort clause כִּֽי נִחַ֤ם יְהוָה֙ עַמּ֔וֹ (oshb:Isa.49.13, byte) is BYTE-IDENTICAL to כִּֽי נִחַ֤ם יְהוָה֙ עַמּ֔וֹ (oshb:Isa.52.9, byte) -- verified as a literal substring of both source verses -- and consonantal search puts that clause in exactly 2 verses book-wide, MT 49:13 and MT 52:9, skeleton tier, verse counts. The second parallel is real and the challenge was tier-honest in declining to call it byte-identical: רָנּ֤וּ שָׁמַ֨יִם֙ (oshb:Isa.49.13, byte) against רָנּ֨וּ שָׁמַ֜יִם (oshb:Isa.44.23, byte) differ in cantillation, as do וּפִצְח֥וּ הָרִ֖ים רִנָּ֑ה (oshb:Isa.49.13, byte) and פִּצְח֤וּ הָרִים֙ רִנָּ֔ה (oshb:Isa.44.23, byte), while the sing-heavens and break-out-mountains verb pair stands in exactly 2 verses book-wide at skeleton tier, verse counts, MT 44:23 and MT 49:13. What the row already does correctly and must keep through repair: the splice carries the staged doubled pair יפצחו וּפִצְח֥וּ (oshb:Isa.49.13, byte), the unpointed written form beside the pointed read form, so the engagement holds both forms instead of resolving one away, and the SAMEKH at MT 49:13 is cited under its exact type, single-witness.

Replace the process-precedent clause in P14-004.strongest_rejected_alternative with the byte warrant: the comfort clause כִּֽי נִחַ֤ם יְהוָה֙ עַמּ֔וֹ (oshb:Isa.49.13) is byte-identical to the clause in the doxological call at oshb:Isa.52.9 (skeleton: 2 verses book-wide, verse counts), and the same imperative verb pair opens oshb:Isa.44.23, רָנּ֨וּ שָׁמַ֜יִם and פִּצְח֤וּ הָרִים֙ רִנָּ֔ה, which is a vocabulary parallel at skeleton tier (2 verses book-wide) and explicitly NOT byte-identical, the accents differing. rulings.challenge_claim: Isolating the narrated complaint is defensible on voice, but the row omits the strongest byte device crossing its own back seam -- the forget-root chain binding complaint to answer -- and one stated seam ground, that the next verse opens a new second-person address, is imprecise.
rulings.grounds: Both limbs verify on the bytes, with the digits and the count-objects reproducing exactly. The chain is byte-real and straddles this one-verse span's own back seam: oshb:Isa.49.14 closes שְׁכֵחָֽנִי (byte), one token, and the adjoining oshb:Isa.49.15 carries three, opening הֲתִשְׁכַּ֤ח אִשָּׁה֙ עוּלָ֔הּ (byte), continuing תִשְׁכַּ֔חְנָה (byte) and closing אֶשְׁכָּחֵֽךְ (byte) -- four occurrences of the root across the two adjacent verses. Consonantal search returns exactly 9 verses book-wide (MT 17:10, 23:15, 23:16, 49:14, 49:15, 51:13, 54:4, 65:11, 65:16), skeleton tier, verse counts, and exactly 2 of them fall in this chapter: these two. A byte-true lexical chain straddling a row's own seam argues continuity against the cut unless disclosed, and the rival field does consider the merge but rests only on the voice contrast and never names the device, so the rival is disclosed while its actual evidence is not. The second limb also verifies: oshb:Isa.49.15 opens הֲתִשְׁכַּ֤ח אִשָּׁה֙ עוּלָ֔הּ (byte), a third-person rhetorical question about a woman and the son of her womb, and its only second-person element is the closing suffix in אֶשְׁכָּחֵֽךְ, so 'opens a new second-person address' misdescribes what opens that verse. Neither limb unseats the reading, and the severity assigned is right: the speech-attribution reading is byte-true, oshb:Isa.49.14 opening וַתֹּ֥אמֶר צִיּ֖וֹן (byte), a wayyiqtol with a named subject; the deviation from the chapter's default category is disclosed under the operative-category allowance; the SAMEKH at MT 49:13 is correctly typed and single-witness-disclosed; and no mark falls inside the span, absence never being counterevidence.
rulings.remedy: Author-wave work order, disclosure only (no boundary change). (i) In P14-005.strongest_rejected_alternative, disclose the cross-seam chain with its bytes and tier: שְׁכֵחָֽנִי (oshb:Isa.49.14) against הֲתִשְׁכַּ֤ח אִשָּׁה֙ עוּלָ֔הּ, תִשְׁכַּ֔חְנָה and אֶשְׁכָּחֵֽךְ (oshb:Isa.49.15), four occurrences across the two adjacent verses, consonantal sweep 9 verses book-wide with 2 in this chapter (skeleton tier, verse counts), and state the ground on which the voice contrast outweighs it. (ii) Re-cut the back-seam sentence to name what actually opens oshb:Isa.49.15 -- a third-person rhetorical question -- with the second-person element identified as the closing suffix rather than the verse's opening. Add oshb:Isa.49.15 to boundary_evidence_refs. Tests the cure must pass, being the tests that killed the original: no byte-true device straddling the row's own seam is left undisclosed; every statement about a neighbouring verse's form names that verse's actual opening tokens; every digit names its swept object and unit; the ref-mirror check stays green with oshb:Isa.49.15 mirrored; splices re-collate byte with the normalization dry-run clean.

rulings.challenge_claim: OL: the rationale's denial that any fresh imperative divides this span is byte-false, since oshb:Isa.49.18 opens with a paired feminine-singular imperative, the same device class this cluster treats as a tier-1 driver five verses earlier, while the disclosed rival rests instead on the oath signature in that verse, which is not a boundary candidate. LF: the rejected-alternative discussion names a candidate boundary with the artifact term row instead of by verse.
rulings.grounds: Distinct items: one byte defect, one register claim that does not hold. OL UPHELD IN FULL. oshb:Isa.49.18 opens שְׂאִֽי סָבִ֤יב עֵינַ֨יִךְ֙ וּרְאִ֔י (byte) -- two feminine-singular imperatives bracketing the addressed object, rendered as commands by the English witness as well -- so the rationale's universal, that no fresh imperative, vocative or messenger formula divides this run of second-person address, is BYTE-FALSE inside the row's own span, and it is falsified by the very device class the adjoining one-verse doxology uses as its tier-1 driver five verses earlier. The rival field does single out this verse, but only through the oath signature חַי אָ֣נִי נְאֻם יְהוָ֗ה (oshb:Isa.49.18, byte), which it correctly holds as postpositive: that signature belongs to the oracle-signature census of 23 verses book-wide (verse counts), MT 49:18 among them, and is never an onset frame. So the disclosed rival rests on the one device in that verse that is NOT a boundary candidate while the device that is goes unnamed. What survives and must not be discarded in repair: the PE at MT 49:21 is correctly typed and is the only mark in the span; the messenger frame at oshb:Isa.49.22 is byte-true as the next onset; and the second-person feminine address does run unbroken across MT 49:15-49:21, verified token by token in every verse of the run -- אֶשְׁכָּחֵֽךְ (oshb:Isa.49.15), חַקֹּתִ֑יךְ (oshb:Isa.49.16), בָּנָ֑יִךְ (oshb:Isa.49.17), עֵינַ֨יִךְ֙ (oshb:Isa.49.18), חָרְבֹתַ֨יִךְ֙ (oshb:Isa.49.19), בְאָזְנַ֔יִךְ (oshb:Isa.49.20), בִּלְבָבֵ֗ךְ (oshb:Isa.49.21), all byte -- which is real continuity evidence for the span as a whole and the material for the re-argument. LF LIMB REFUTED: the clause cited, opening a fresh row at web:Isa.49.19, carries an explicit verse anchor and names no position, and the register rule bars positional row references while requiring cross-row references to be verse-anchored -- this clause satisfies both. The positional-reference census confirms it: this row carries ZERO positional row references, against one each in the three sibling rows filed identically in the same packet.
rulings.remedy: Author-wave work order, re-argument and disclosure only; no boundary change is proposed and the span does not move. Replace the universal in P14-006.boundary_rationale with a byte-grounded statement: the verse-initial feminine-singular imperative pair שְׂאִֽי סָבִ֤יב עֵינַ֨יִךְ֙ וּרְאִ֔י (oshb:Isa.49.18) does stand inside the span, and the ground on which it is a turn within the continuing address rather than a fresh onset is the unbroken second-person feminine address across oshb:Isa.49.15-Isa.49.21, with a token present in every verse of the run. Keep the postpositive oath reading of חַי אָ֣נִי נְאֻם יְהוָ֗ה but move it out of the rival slot, since the imperative and not the signature is the real declined candidate. Add oshb:Isa.49.18 to boundary_evidence_refs. No register edit is owed on this row. Tests the cure must pass, being the test that killed the original: no universal survives that a form standing inside the row's own span falsifies; the rival field names the strongest declined device and shows its form; the mark-symmetry sweep stays green with PE never conflated with SAMEKH; every splice re-collates byte with the normalization dry-run clean; and if the imperative cannot be sustained as a within-address turn, confidence drops rather than the sentence being kept.

rulings.challenge_claim: OL: the boundary survives on its messenger frame, but the declared driver -- an addressee shift to the nations -- is byte-false, the second-person feminine addressee being Zion, unbroken from the preceding span, and with device notes empty the continuing feminine address across the front seam is undisclosed. LF: the rejected-alternative discussion names the preceding unit with the artifact term row rather than by content.
rulings.grounds: Distinct items. OL UPHELD, verified token by token. Across oshb:Isa.49.22-Isa.49.23 every second-person form is feminine singular and continues the addressee of the preceding unit: בָנַ֨יִךְ֙ and וּבְנֹתַ֖יִךְ (oshb:Isa.49.22, byte); אֹֽמְנַ֗יִךְ, מֵינִ֣יקֹתַ֔יִךְ, רַגְלַ֖יִךְ and the perfect וְיָדַ֨עַתְּ֙ כִּֽי אֲנִ֣י יְהוָ֔ה (oshb:Isa.49.23, byte). The nations are the goal and the third-person agents of the sentence -- אֶל גּוֹיִם֙ and וְאֶל עַמִּ֖ים (oshb:Isa.49.22, byte) with a plural verb of bringing -- never the addressee. That feminine-singular address runs continuously from MT 49:15 through MT 49:23, a token present in every verse of the run, so 'addressed to the nations rather than continuing the report of what Zion herself will say' misstates what changes at the seam, and the declared addressee-shift signal, a dependent field of the driver, does not survive with it as written. What does hold at byte tier is the verse-initial divine messenger frame כֹּֽה אָמַ֞ר אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהוִ֗ה (oshb:Isa.49.22, byte), an inventoried divine frame and not one of the four royal-messenger sites, a sufficient tier-1 onset on its own, so the cut itself is not in question -- only its stated ground and its declared signal. FRAMING REFINED: there IS a real shift at this seam, just not the one named. The preceding verse is Zion's own quoted words, וְאָמַ֣רְתְּ בִּלְבָבֵ֗ךְ (oshb:Isa.49.21, byte), and the seam turns from her reported speech back to divine speech about her; the correction re-describes the shift rather than deleting it. With device_notes empty, the continuing feminine address across the front seam is undisclosed, which is the same omission the adjoining row shows from the other side. LF LIMB UPHELD BUT AT LOW: 'Extending the preceding row' is a genuine positional reference, though the verse anchor the challenge credits is present; the class is corpus-wide at 32 positional occurrences in 24 of 225 rows, so the cure is the corpus-wide register pass and not a medium c22 finding.
rulings.remedy: Author-wave work order; driver re-argument, disclosure and register, with no boundary change and no movement of the span. (i) Re-cut the driver in P14-007.boundary_rationale to what the bytes carry: the verse-initial frame כֹּֽה אָמַ֞ר אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהוִ֗ה (oshb:Isa.49.22) plus the turn from Zion's own quoted words at oshb:Isa.49.21 back to divine speech about her, stating explicitly that the second-person feminine addressee is unchanged and that the nations stand as goal and third-person agents. Because observed_substrate_signals is a dependent field of the driver, re-derive the signal set from the corrected driver and re-open strongest_rejected_alternative, unit_type and confidence with it. (ii) Fill device_notes with the cross-seam disclosure of the continuing feminine address across oshb:Isa.49.15-Isa.49.23, tokens present in every verse. (iii) Apply the corpus-wide register pass to the positional reference. Add oshb:Isa.49.21 to boundary_evidence_refs. Tests the cure must pass, being the tests that killed the original: the declared driver is re-derived from the bytes and every dependent field is re-checked against it, not left standing; no cross-seam continuity device is left undisclosed on either side of the seam; the mark-symmetry sweep stays green with the PE at MT 49:21 and the SAMEKH at MT 49:23 correctly typed and never conflated; the ref-mirror check stays green; every splice re-collates byte with the normalization dry-run clean.

rulings.challenge_claim: OL: the row's own closing device is half of a byte-true recognition-formula pair bracketing across its front seam (a consonantal sweep of the shared core returning 4 verses book-wide), a weaker redeemer chain runs the length of the cluster undisclosed, and the verse-initial divine frame sitting inside the span at oshb:Isa.49.25 is never argued from the bytes that would make it non-boundary. LF: the rejected-alternative discussion names the preceding unit with the artifact term row rather than by content.
rulings.grounds: Three limbs verify as observations; one ships a digit that reproduces under no count-object. LIMB 1, OBSERVATION UPHELD, DIGIT REFUTED. The formula closing this span, וְיָדְע֣וּ כָל בָּשָׂ֗ר כִּ֣י אֲנִ֤י יְהוָה֙ (oshb:Isa.49.26, byte), shares its core with the formula closing the unit that ends at oshb:Isa.49.23, וְיָדַ֨עַתְּ֙ כִּֽי אֲנִ֣י יְהוָ֔ה (byte), and a device bracketing across the seam at Isa.49.23|Isa.49.24 argues for one larger unit across it, disclosed on neither side -- this row's device_notes reads None. But the cited sweep of 4 verses book-wide reproduces under no object: the shared core itself returns 7 verses book-wide (MT 41:13, 43:3, 45:3, 49:23, 49:26, 60:16, 61:8), the narrower recognition formula with its perfect returns 2 (MT 49:23, 60:16), and the savior-title extension returns 2 (MT 49:26, 60:16) -- all skeleton tier, verse counts, none of them 4. A digit that names no reproducing swept object is the count-object defect the campaign's own count discipline forbids, and it must not be carried into the author wave; the bracketing observation survives with the corrected figure. LIMB 2 UPHELD EXACTLY: כִּי כֹ֣ה אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֗ה (oshb:Isa.49.25, byte) is verse-initial and an inventoried divine frame, the identical device class used as the tier-1 boundary driver at MT 49:7, 49:8, 49:22 and 50:1, and the row's rendering does carry the causal particle that is the real discriminator but never argues from it, so one driver is applied at four seams and silently withheld at a fifth. LIMB 3 UPHELD EXACTLY: גֹּאֵ֨ל (oshb:Isa.49.7, byte) and the suffixed וְגֹאֲלֵ֖ךְ (oshb:Isa.49.26, byte) are the only two sites of that root in chapters 49-50, consonantal sweep 21 verses book-wide, verse counts. LF LIMB UPHELD AT LOW: 'the preceding row' is a genuine positional reference inside the corpus-wide class of 32 occurrences in 24 of 225 rows, and the verse anchor is present, so the cure is the register pass rather than a medium c22 finding. What holds and must be preserved: the interrogative onset הֲיֻקַּ֥ח מִגִּבּ֖וֹר (oshb:Isa.49.24, byte) is byte-true and the SAMEKH marks at both edges are correctly typed and single-witness-disclosed.
rulings.remedy: Author-wave work order, disclosure and register only (no boundary change). (i) Disclose the recognition-formula bracket in device_notes with both forms spliced and a CORRECTED count-object: וְיָדַ֨עַתְּ֙ כִּֽי אֲנִ֣י יְהוָ֔ה (oshb:Isa.49.23) and וְיָדְע֣וּ כָל בָּשָׂ֗ר כִּ֣י אֲנִ֤י יְהוָה֙ (oshb:Isa.49.26), the shared core standing in 7 verses book-wide and the recognition formula with the perfect in 2 (skeleton tier, verse counts) -- never the unreproducible figure of 4 -- and give the ground on which the interrogative onset at oshb:Isa.49.24 outweighs the bracket. Mirror that disclosure on the other side of the Isa.49.23|Isa.49.24 seam as ONE seam-pair edit, not two. (ii) Argue the interior frame from its bytes: כִּי כֹ֣ה אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֗ה (oshb:Isa.49.25) is an inventoried divine frame whose causal particle marks it as the answering frame to the question at oshb:Isa.49.24 rather than a fresh onset. (iii) If the redeemer chain is to be claimed at all, write it with its object and digit: גֹּאֵ֨ל (oshb:Isa.49.7) and וְגֹאֲלֵ֖ךְ (oshb:Isa.49.26), the only two sites in chapters 49-50, skeleton sweep 21 verses book-wide, and add oshb:Isa.49.7 to boundary_evidence_refs. (iv) Apply the corpus-wide register pass to the positional reference. Tests the cure must pass, being the tests that killed the original: no digit ships without a named swept object that actually reproduces it; every cross-seam device is disclosed on both sides as one edit; the frame-ownership census is named wherever a messenger-formula site is engaged; the ref-mirror check stays green with any new out-of-span ref mirrored; every splice re-collates byte with the normalization dry-run clean.

rulings.challenge_claim: The closing seam of this span is carried by a single-witness parashah mark plus a content observation, with no tier-1 byte signal named, although one sits in the next verse; and the pointed splice offered for oshb:Isa.50.2 is the whole verse while the paired English rendering is only the mid-verse clause, so quote and gloss are not cut to the same measure.
rulings.grounds: Both limbs verify, and the framing needs one correction plus one binding caution. The back-seam sentence offers only a content observation and the SAMEKH at MT 50:3; the parashah layer in the Prophets is tier-3 weak single-witness corroboration and never a boundary driver, so the closing seam ships with no tier-1 ground, and no ref beyond the span appears in boundary_evidence_refs to supply one. The bytes do supply it: oshb:Isa.50.4 opens אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהֹוִ֗ה נָ֤תַן לִי֙ (byte), a fronted divine title with a first-person recipient, turning from the divine first-person speech of this span to a first-person report about the speaker, and both witnesses render that turn alike. The quote/gloss residue also verifies: the pointed splice for oshb:Isa.50.2 is the whole 28-token verse opening מַדּ֨וּעַ while the English clause quoted beside it is only the mid-verse shortened-hand question, so the two are not cut to the same measure. FRAMING REFINED and severity lowered to low: this is a missing corroboration citation at one seam, not a seam without warrant. The front bound and the form-class tagging are byte-solid -- oshb:Isa.50.1 opens כֹּ֣ה אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֗ה (byte), verse-initial and an inventoried divine frame, and the interrogative chain is byte-present across the span, אֵ֣י זֶ֠ה and א֚וֹ מִ֣י (oshb:Isa.50.1, byte), מַדּ֨וּעַ and הֲקָצ֨וֹר (oshb:Isa.50.2, byte) -- so the form change at Isa.50.3|Isa.50.4 is byte-real and merely uncited, and the SAMEKH at MT 49:26 is correctly typed at the front. HELD-OPEN CAUTION, binding on the cure: citing the onset at oshb:Isa.50.4 as the tier-1 ground for a division the row set has already made is disclosure of an existing seam, and it must not be written so as to settle how far the Isa.50.4-Isa.50.11 material attaches, nor to touch the servant referent -- both are held opens that no row and no remedy decides. The row's own device_notes correctly holds the identity of the mother rather than adjudicating it, and that discipline stands.
rulings.remedy: Author-wave work order, disclosure only (no boundary change; the span does not move and no attachment question is settled). (i) Add the tier-1 back-seam ground with its bytes: this span's divine first-person speech closes at oshb:Isa.50.3 and oshb:Isa.50.4 opens אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהֹוִ֗ה נָ֤תַן לִי֙, a fronted divine title with a first-person recipient, a form change both witnesses render alike; add web:Isa.50.4 and oshb:Isa.50.4 to boundary_evidence_refs, keeping the SAMEKH at MT 50:3 as tier-3 single-witness corroboration explicitly named as not the driver. (ii) Re-cut the paired citation at oshb:Isa.50.2 to one measure: either quote the whole verse from the English witness or splice only the shortened-hand clause, הֲקָצ֨וֹר onward, so quote and gloss cover the same span. (iii) The cure must NOT state or imply where the Isa.50.4-Isa.50.11 material attaches, and must not name or decide the speaker there. Tests the cure must pass, being the tests that killed the original: no seam ships with a parashah mark as its only corroboration and no tier-1 ground named; quote and gloss cover the same span at every paired citation; the ref-mirror check stays green with the new out-of-span ref mirrored; every splice re-collates byte with the normalization dry-run clean; and the coda attachment and the servant referent remain undecided in every field.
